The '''2024 Cheltenham Borough Council election''' was held on Thursday 2 May 2024, alongside the [[2024 United Kingdom local elections|other local elections in the United Kingdom]] being held on the same day. All 40 members of [[Cheltenham Borough Council]] in [[Gloucestershire]] were elected following boundary changes.

The Liberal Democrats retained control of the local authority.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-03 |title=Cheltenham Council held by Lib Dems as Tories lose seats |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cmj61dk78m3o |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}</ref> The Conservatives were [[Wipeout (elections)|wiped out]] losing all their seats on the council, with the Greens replacing them as the largest opposition party.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Norris |first=Phil |last2=Garcia |first2=Carmelo |date=2024-05-03 |title=Cheltenham Borough Council local election results and reaction - updates |url=https://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/news/cheltenham-news/live-cheltenham-borough-council-local-9260794 |access-date=2024-05-09 |website=Gloucestershire Live |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=ELECTION RESULTS: No singing for the blues in Cheltenham|first1=Simon|last1=Hacker|website=Punchline-Gloucester.com|access-date=20 May 2024|date=4 May 2024 |url=https://www.punchline-gloucester.com/articles/aanews/conservatives-suffer-wipeout-in-cheltenham-local-elections}}</ref>

==Background==
Since its creation in 1974, control of the council has alternated between the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] and [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Cheltenham Borough Council Election Results 1973-2012 |url=http://www.electionscentre.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/Cheltenham-1973-2012.pdf |website=Elections Centre |access-date=29 February 2024}}</ref> The Conservatives controlled the council until [[1979 Cheltenham Borough Council election|1979]], when it fell into [[no overall control]] until [[1991 Cheltenham Borough Council election|1991]], when the Liberal Democrats took control. The Conservatives briefly controlled the council from [[2000 Cheltenham Borough Council election|2000]] to [[2002 Cheltenham Borough Council election|2002]], with the Liberal Democrats re-taking control from no overall control in [[2010 Cheltenham Borough Council election|2010]]. The Liberal Democrats have formed majority administrations since then.

In the [[2022 Cheltenham Borough Council election|most recent election]], the Liberal Democrats maintained their seat count with 55.1% of the vote, the Conservatives won 1 seat (down 1) with 27.7%, [[People Against Bureaucracy]] kept their 1-seat up for election with 2.8%, and the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] gained 1 seat with 11.3%.

==Boundary changes==
Cheltenham usually elects its councillors in halves, on a 4-year cycle. However, following boundary changes, all councillors will be elected to the new wards.<ref>{{Cite legislation UK |type=si |year=2023 |number=820 |si= The Cheltenham (Electoral Changes) Order 2023 |accessdate=29 February 2024 }}</ref> All wards have 2 councillors.

Changes:
* June 2022: Wendy Flynn joins Green Party from Liberal Democrats<ref>{{cite news |last1=Garcia |first1=Carmelo |title=Racism fears force town councillor to defect to rival group |url=https://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/news/cheltenham-news/racism-fears-force-town-councillor-7173046 |access-date=29 February 2024 |work=Gloucestershire Live |date=8 June 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
* October 2022: Sandra Holliday suspended from Liberal Democrats<ref>{{cite news |last1=Garcia |first1=Carmelo |title=Town mayor suspended by party over 'disciplinary matter' |url=https://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/news/cheltenham-news/cheltenham-mayor-suspended-party-over-7686641 |access-date=29 February 2024 |work=Gloucestershire Live |date=11 October 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
* December 2022: Louis Savage (Conservative) resigns; by-election held February 2023<ref>{{cite news |last1=Garcia |first1=Carmelo |title='Excellent' doctor councillor stands down sparking by-election |url=https://www.gloucestershirelive.co.uk/news/cheltenham-news/excellent-conservative-councillor-stands-down-7938689 |work=Gloucestershire Live |date=18 December 2022 |language=en}}</ref>
* February 2023: Ed Chidley (Liberal Democrats) wins by-election from the Conservatives<ref>{{cite web |title=Local Elections Archive Project — Battledown Ward |url=https://www.andrewteale.me.uk/leap/ward/5987/#2023-02-09 |website=www.andrewteale.me.uk |access-date=29 February 2024}}</ref>
